Brian L. Schwalb

Democratic candidate for Attorney General for the District of Columbia · Incumbent

Attorney General of the District of Columbia (incumbent); attorney

Brian L. Schwalb is a Democrat who has served as the District of Columbia's elected Attorney General since January 2, 2023, after winning the 2022 general election. He won the June 2026 Democratic primary against Advisory Neighborhood Commissioner J.P. Szymkowicz. He faces Republican Manuel Rivera in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Schwalb stands

Juvenile crime
Says young people must face consequences when they break the law. Says his office has prosecuted serious and violent juvenile offenses at a rate of nearly 85% while working to keep young people from reoffending.
Second-term priorities
Says his goals for a second term are to make DC safer, stronger and more affordable. Lists prosecuting violent juvenile offenses, protecting children from companies, holding Maryland and Virginia drivers accountable, and enforcing environmental laws.
Federal National Guard deployment in DC
Brought a lawsuit to end the federal government's National Guard deployment in the District, which his office calls illegal. The case is being argued before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit.
Worker and tenant protection
Has filed wage theft lawsuits, including one against a childcare center accused of not paying six workers when it closed. Has also sued landlords over building disrepair and safety conditions.
Public corruption
Announced public corruption charges against six Metropolitan Police Department members accused of an overtime fraud scheme.
